body_long:
On the shores of Lake Geneva, Switzerland's top-ranked golf course is preparing for its biggest change in four decades. The Golf Club du Domaine Impérial, at Gland, announced on 25 November 2026 that it is renovating all 18 holes at the same time, and confirmed Thomas Benassayag as its general manager.

## A Pete Dye course, rebuilt at once

The course was designed by Pete Dye and officially opened in May 1988 with a long drive by Severiano Ballesteros. The club says it is the only course in Europe designed entirely by Dye, and Top 100 Golf Courses ranks it first in Switzerland, a position it has held for several editions.

Renovating every hole simultaneously is rare at this level. The club describes the work as a project of a scale seldom seen in Europe. The brief is twofold: keep the character of Dye's original layout, and prepare the course for the environmental demands of the coming decades. That means lower water consumption, fewer plant-protection products and maintenance that favours biodiversity.

The timing is deliberate. The club, founded in 1987, will celebrate its 40th anniversary in 2027 with a year of events. Its clubhouse is Villa Prangins, a lakeside residence built in the 1860s for Prince Jérôme Napoléon, on an estate whose history goes back to the 17th century. Close to 1,000 members belong to the club.

## A hotelier at the helm

Thomas Benassayag took office on 1 September 2026. He trained at the École Hôtelière de Strasbourg and at EHL in Lausanne, then spent around fifteen years in management roles across hotels, restaurants and luxury hospitality consulting in France, China and the United States, notably with Sofitel and Mandarin Oriental. A keen golfer, he then became general manager of the Opio-Valbonne Golf Resort, near Cannes, where he built an offer that combined golf, hospitality, dining, wellness and events.

His stated ambition is to make the Domaine Impérial an international reference for the golf experience and for high-end club life, building on the club's heritage, its teams and the unique identity of its lakeside setting. The club's committee points to his background in luxury hotels and in running a golf resort.

## The signal

The best private clubs are borrowing from luxury hotels. A great course is no longer enough: members judge the service, the table and the setting as much as the greens. Hiring a palace-trained hotelier to steer a heritage course through a full rebuild shows where the bar now sits.

Congratulations to Thomas Benassayag and the Domaine Impérial teams.

summary: The Pete Dye course on Lake Geneva, ranked first in Switzerland, is renovating all 18 holes ahead of its 40th anniversary in 2027, with Thomas Benassayag as general manager.
title: Domaine Impérial, Switzerland's top golf club, renovates all 18 holes before turning 40
why: A hotelier from Sofitel and Mandarin Oriental takes Switzerland's No. 1 course into its 40th year.
